bear_case.title: China dominates cells — and domestic rivalry is compressing terms further
bear_case.description: CATL still holds the global No.1 BESS shipment position for H1 2026 (storage now 19.23% of its revenue), and just locked in a 10-year, up-to-200GWh supply deal with Beijing HyperStrong running through 2028 — deepening its grip on the value chain. BYD and Sungrow's earlier win of the Masdar deal already showed domestic rivalry compresses terms on its own; combined, CATL and BYD now account for 62.43% of battery installations, the highest concentration in recent months.

bear_case.title: Tariffs keep rising, and FEOC/FERC rules add layers of cost and complexity
bear_case.description: Section 301 duties on Chinese-origin ESS batteries jumped from 40.9% in 2025 to 58.4% in 2026, and FEOC content thresholds (55% domestic in 2026, rising to 75% after 2029) still risk disqualifying projects from the ITC. Layered on top, the FERC-directed PJM co-location rule rewrite remains mid-implementation in 2026 — transmission cost allocation under the new framework directly affects grid-services revenue for data-center-adjacent storage names like NRGV and Cummins' customers.

bear_case.title: Fluence's crisis has become a litigation and credibility problem for the whole stack
bear_case.description: Beyond the $600M guidance cut and the disclosed SEC investigation, Fluence faces a securities class action (lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 27) alleging its plan relied on Houston capacity that was not operating. Shares ($5.80) closed at a new 12-month low on Oct 16, Morgan Stanley and Susquehanna cut targets this week, and Eos ($1.82, -15.7% on Oct 16) now faces multiple law-firm investigations. The market is repricing execution risk for any integrator that depends on US contract-manufacturing ramps.

bear_case.title: Solid-state timelines keep slipping while China's catches up
bear_case.description: QuantumScape shares ($4.01) sit near their 52-week low, with Morgan Stanley cutting its target to $4.50 from $8.50; the PowerCo licensing deal still targets only a 2027 commercial launch with no revenue yet. CATL and BYD are both still publicly targeting 2027 solid-state trial production, meaning the assumed Western first-mover advantage in solid-state keeps eroding rather than firming up.
